sections.content: After recomendar *que*, aconsejar que and similar expressions, the present subjunctive normally introduces the recommended action. This is especially clear when the person giving the recommendation and the person who should act are different.

items.spanish: Te recomiendo que hables con alguien que conozca bien el problema.
items.english: I recommend that you speak to someone who knows the problem well.

items.spanish: El médico aconseja que evitemos el ejercicio durante unos días.
items.english: The doctor advises that we avoid exercise for a few days.

items.spanish: Te recomiendo que no tomes una decisión mientras estés enfadado.
items.english: I recommend that you do not make a decision while you are angry.

items.spanish: Les aconsejamos que comparen las alternativas antes de elegir.
items.english: We advise them to compare the alternatives before choosing.

sections.content: When the recommendation is directed at another subject, use *que* + present subjunctive. If the same person performs both actions, an infinitive is often more natural.
